first: श्री विद्यां जगतां धात्रीं सर्गस्स्थि लयेश्वरीम् ।
en: I bow to Lalita, the eternal Mahatripurasundari. She is Shri Vidya itself, she upholds the worlds, and she rules over their creation, keeping and dissolving.
Agastya said: O horse-faced Hayagriva, wise one, master of all the scriptures, you have told me the most wonderful story of the goddess Lalita.
You told me in detail how the Mother first appeared, how she was then crowned, and how she killed the demon Bhanda.
You also described Shripura, her city of great splendour, and the glory of the holy fifteen-syllable mantra.
In the section on nyasa you explained the six-fold nyasa and the other ways of placing the mantra on the body, and also the order of inner worship and outer worship.
In the section on worship you described the order of the great worship, and in the section on purashcharana you explained the rules of japa, the repeating of the mantra.
In the section on homa you told the method and the materials for the fire offering. You also spoke of the Shri Chakra, the mantra, the goddess and the guru,
and in the secret section you explained how these are one with each other. In the section of hymns you gave many kinds of praises.
In the section of thousand names you told the names of the goddesses Mantrini and Dandini, but you did not tell the thousand names of the goddess Lalita herself.

first: तत्र मे संशयो जातो हयग्रीव दयानिधे ।
en: O Hayagriva, ocean of mercy, a doubt has come to my mind about this. Did you forget it, or did you know it and leave it out on purpose?

first: मम वा योग्यता नास्ति श्रोतुं नामसहस्रकम् ।
en: Or am I not fit to hear these thousand names? Tell me the reason why you did not speak of them.
Suta said: When the sage born from a pot, Agastya, asked this, Hayagriva was very pleased and spoke to the ascetic.
Shri Hayagriva said: O Agastya, husband of Lopamudra, listen with full attention. I will tell you why I did not speak of the thousand names.
I did not tell them only because I held them to be a secret, and for no other reason. Since you ask again with devotion, I will now tell you.
A teacher may tell even a secret to a devoted disciple. But you must never give it to someone who has no devotion.

first: न शठाय न दुष्टाय नाविश्वासाय कर्हिचित् ।
en: Never give it to a cheat, a wicked person or one without faith. Give it to one who loves the holy Mother and knows Shri Vidya, the king of mantras,
to a pure worshipper; to such a person these thousand names may be given. Among all the thousand-name hymns, which surely bring quick success,
this is the chief one for the goddess Lalita in the tantras, O sage. Just as Shri Vidya is the highest of mantras, and within it the form beginning with 'ka' is the highest,
as Shripura is the best of cities, as Lalita is the first among the goddesses, and as Shiva is the highest god for the worshippers of Shri Vidya,
so this is declared the best among thousand-name hymns. The goddess Lalitambika is pleased by the reading of it
in a way she is not pleased by the reading of any other thousand-name hymn. So, to please the holy Mother, one should recite this every day.
One who worships Lalitambika in the Shri Chakra with these thousand names, offering bilva leaves, lotuses or tulasi flowers,
receives the grace of the Queen of the lion throne at once. After worshipping the Shri Chakra and repeating the fifteen-syllable mantra,
one should recite these thousand names daily at the end of the japa. If one is not able to do japa and worship, one should simply read the thousand names.
Then one gets the same fruit as from full worship and full japa. Reading other hymns in worship brings only worldly gain.
One should recite these thousand names as a daily duty. Worship of the goddess in the Shri Chakra, japa of her mantra, and reciting her names:
this much is the duty of a devotee; anything more is for extra gain. Reciting these thousand names is necessary for a devotee. Listen, Agastya, and I will tell you the reason.
Long ago the goddess Shri Lalita, wishing to help her devotees,
called the goddesses of speech, led by Vashini, and said: 'Goddesses of speech, Vashini and the rest, listen to my words.'
'By my grace you have rich powers of speech, and I have given you the task of granting the gift of speech to my devotees.'
'You know the secret of my chakra and you are devoted to my names. So I command you to make a hymn in my praise.'
'Make a hymn marked with my thousand names, so that when devotees praise me with it I am at once greatly pleased.'
Hayagriva said: Commanded in this way by the goddess Shri Lalitamba, the goddesses of speech made a hymn without equal, with divine and secret names.
It became famous as the supreme Secret Thousand Names. Then once, the Mother sat on her lion throne in her court
and gave everyone the chance to serve her, O Agastya. Millions of Brahmas came there to serve,
millions of Lakshmis and Narayanas came, and millions of Rudras came together with millions of Gauris.
The Shaktis of many forms, led by Mantrini and Dandini, also came to serve; their number cannot be counted.
The divine, human and perfected lines of teachers came too. There the goddess Shri Lalita showed herself to all.

first: तेषु दुष्टोपविष्टेषु स्वे स्वे स्थाने यथाक्रमम् ।
en: When they had seen her and sat down in their own places in proper order, then, moved by a side glance from the goddess Shri Lalita,
Vashini and the other goddesses of speech stood up with folded hands and praised Lalitambika with the thousand names they had made.
Hearing the hymn, Lalita, the supreme goddess, was pleased, and everyone in the court was filled with wonder.
Then Lalita said to the gods in her court: 'It was by my command that the goddesses of speech made this hymn without equal.'
'It is marked with divine names that please me. Always read this hymn to increase my joy.'
'Spread my thousand names among the devotees. The devotee who reads my thousand names even once'

first: स मे प्रियतमो ज्ञेयस्तस्मै कामान् ददाम्यहम् ।
en: 'should be known as most dear to me, and I grant that person's wishes. After worshipping me in the Shri Chakra and repeating the fifteen-syllable mantra,'
'one should then recite my thousand names to please me. Whether one worships me or not, whether one repeats the mantra or not,'
'one should always recite these thousand names for my pleasure. Out of love for me, all of you, always recite them with respect.'
Hayagriva said: In this way Shri Lalita, the ruling goddess, instructed the gods and their followers.
From that time, by her command, Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, and the Shaktis led by Mantrini, read these thousand names
with devotion always, to please Lalita. So, O sage, a devotee must surely recite this hymn.
O best of sages, I have told you why it is necessary. Now I will tell you the thousand names; listen with faith.
